questions.question: What time period does classical antiquity cover?
options: Between the 8th century BC and the 5th century AD
Between the 5th century BC and the 8th century AD
Between the 10th century BC and the 3rd century AD
Between the 3rd century BC and the 7th century AD
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that classical antiquity is the period between the 8th century BC and the 5th century AD.
Incorrect. The article specifies the period as between the 8th century BC and the 5th century AD, not the 5th century BC to the 8th century AD.
Incorrect. The article specifies the period as between the 8th century BC and the 5th century AD, not the 10th century BC to the 3rd century AD.
Incorrect. The article specifies the period as between the 8th century BC and the 5th century AD, not the 3rd century BC to the 7th century AD.

questions.question: Which two civilizations are known together as the Greco-Roman world?
options: Ancient Greece and Rome
Ancient Egypt and Greece
Ancient Persia and Rome
Ancient Greece and Carthage
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the interwoven civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome are known together as the Greco-Roman world.
Incorrect. The article identifies ancient Greece and Rome, not ancient Egypt and Greece, as the Greco-Roman world.
Incorrect. The article identifies ancient Greece and Rome, not ancient Persia and Rome, as the Greco-Roman world.
Incorrect. The article identifies ancient Greece and Rome, not ancient Greece and Carthage, as the Greco-Roman world.

questions.question: According to the article, what event conventionally marks the end of classical antiquity?
options: The fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD
The death of Alexander the Great in 323 BC
The founding of Rome in 753 BC
The Roman conquest of Greece in 146 BC
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that classical antiquity conventionally ends with the fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD.
Incorrect. The death of Alexander the Great marks the end of the classical Greek period, not the end of classical antiquity.
Incorrect. The founding of Rome is a beginning point, not the end of classical antiquity.
Incorrect. The Roman conquest of Greece marks the end of the Hellenistic period, not the end of classical antiquity.

questions.question: What did the Romans do with the culture of ancient Greece?
options: They preserved, imitated, and spread it throughout Europe
They completely destroyed it and replaced it with their own
They ignored it and had no influence from it
They only adopted it after conquering Greece in 146 BC
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the Romans preserved, imitated, and spread this culture throughout Europe.
Incorrect. The article states the Romans preserved and spread the culture, not destroyed it.
Incorrect. The article clearly states the Romans were influenced by and spread Greek culture.
Incorrect. The article does not limit Roman adoption of Greek culture to after 146 BC.

questions.question: What revival beginning in the 14th century was helped by surviving fragments of classical culture?
options: The Renaissance
The Enlightenment
The Industrial Revolution
The Reformation
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says surviving fragments of classical culture helped produce a revival beginning during the 14th century, later known as the Renaissance.
Incorrect. The article specifically names the Renaissance, not the Enlightenment.
Incorrect. The article specifically names the Renaissance, not the Industrial Revolution.
Incorrect. The article specifically names the Renaissance, not the Reformation.

questions.question: According to legend, when was Rome founded?
options: On 21 April 753 BC
On 1 January 509 BC
On 15 March 44 BC
On 4 July 776 BC
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says according to legend, Rome was founded on 21 April 753 BC by Romulus and Remus.
Incorrect. 509 BC is the traditional date for the expulsion of the kings and the founding of the Republic, not the founding of Rome.
Incorrect. 44 BC is the year of Julius Caesar's assassination, not the founding of Rome.
Incorrect. 776 BC is the traditional date for the first Olympic Games, not the founding of Rome.

questions.question: What happened to the Roman monarchy after the expulsion of Tarquinius Superbus?
options: The Senate voted to never again allow the rule of a king and reformed Rome into a republic
A new king was immediately chosen from the Etruscans
The Roman Empire was established with an emperor
Rome was ruled by a series of dictators for the next century
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the Senate in 509 BC voted to never again allow the rule of a king and reformed Rome into a republican government.
Incorrect. The article says the Senate voted to never again allow a king, not to choose a new one.
Incorrect. The Roman Empire came much later, not immediately after the expulsion of the kings.
Incorrect. The article says Rome became a republic, not a series of dictatorships.

questions.question: What was the result of the Battle of Leuctra in 371 BC?
options: The end of Spartan supremacy and the establishment of Theban hegemony
The beginning of Athenian dominance in the Delian League
The final victory of the Persians over the Greeks
The unification of Greece under Alexander the Great
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the result of this battle was the end of Spartan supremacy and the establishment of Theban hegemony.
Incorrect. Athenian dominance came earlier with the Delian League, not from this battle.
Incorrect. This battle was between Thebes and Sparta, not the Persians and Greeks.
Incorrect. Alexander the Great came later, and this battle did not unify Greece under him.

questions.question: What language became the lingua franca far beyond Greece during the Hellenistic period?
options: Greek
Latin
Persian
Egyptian
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Greek became the lingua franca far beyond Greece itself during the Hellenistic period.
Incorrect. Latin was the language of the Romans, not the lingua franca of the Hellenistic period.
Incorrect. Persian was the language of the Persian Empire, not the lingua franca of the Hellenistic period.
Incorrect. Egyptian was the language of Egypt, not the lingua franca of the Hellenistic period.

questions.question: What marked the end of the Hellenistic period according to the article?
options: The Roman conquest of Greece in 146 BC
The death of Alexander the Great in 323 BC
The founding of Carthage in 814 BC
The start of the Peloponnesian War in 431 BC
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the Hellenistic period ended with the Roman conquest of Greece in 146 BC.
Incorrect. The death of Alexander marks the beginning of the Hellenistic period, not its end.
Incorrect. The founding of Carthage is much earlier and not related to the end of the Hellenistic period.
Incorrect. The Peloponnesian War was in the Classical Greek period, not the end of the Hellenistic period.
